findings.diagnosis: The prompt underestimates the risk of cutting immediately after a negation or polarity/quantifier token when the continuation supplies its scope, so it keeps cuts that make the prefix assert (or contradict) the wrong proposition on its own.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_738','en_us_648','en_us_1253','en_us_105','en_us_1116','en_us_419']: each sentence places a negation/polarity or comparative/quantifier token (e.g. "does not", "will never", "either ... or", "ban ... from which", "except for", "from ... to ...") directly before a following phrase (measure, time, unit, percentage, or range) that determines the claim's scope; the policy kept the cut after the polarity/quantifier and those positions carried high contradiction and were dropped offline.
findings.type_predicate: A negation or polarity word (not, no, never, except) or a comparative/quantifier phrase (more than, as many as, either/or, from X to Y, except for) is immediately followed by a numeral, a measurement/unit, a time expression, or a prepositional phrase that supplies the scope or limit of that polarity/quantifier.

edit.text: Do not cut immediately after negation or polarity/quantifier words (not, no, never, except, either/or, more than, as many as, from X to Y) when the next phrase supplies scope (numeral, measurement/unit, time phrase, 'in advance', 'from which').
